authorizedBy: docs/post-3f2-generalization-architecture-decision.json section 11 (recommended semantic architecture: Option 2 deterministic completeness cross-check bundled with Option 1 prompt exhaustiveness fix)
establishedRootCauseRestated: definitions[]/rules[]/sharedCapacities[] are already fully unbounded array-typed end to end (compile.ts/types.ts/wire-schema.ts/normalize.ts/ir/types.ts) - no 1-candidate-to-1-claim architecture defect exists. The gap is (a) prompt.ts has an exhaustiveness instruction for RULES but none for DEFINITIONS, with no worked multi-definition example, and (b) no deterministic mechanism notices when compiled definitions[] is a strict subset of what the source declares.
explicitlyNotDone: No splitting every definition into its own discovery candidate
No new schema tables for individual definition candidates
No legal-term dictionary or enumerated covenant-concept list

unitA1_promptExhaustiveness.change: Added a 'MULTIPLE DEFINITIONS' instruction immediately after the existing 'MULTIPLE RULES' instruction, requiring extraction of every materially relevant definition supported by the source and explicitly prohibiting selecting only representative/salient/covenant-relevant ones. Added one synthetic few-shot example ('Zeta Threshold' / 'Zeta Measurement Period' / 'Zeta Excluded Assets') demonstrating one source region producing three independent WireDefinition outputs, including a case where one sibling is COMPLETE, one has no calculationExpression but is still COMPLETE, and one is PARTIAL (UNSUPPORTED dependent terms) - explicitly modeling that per-term sufficiency is independent per term.
unitA1_promptExhaustiveness.domainGenerality: No Riot/Coinbase/benchmark term or section number appears anywhere in the new prompt text or example; verified by an automated grep test (Unit A12).
unitA1_promptExhaustiveness.genericInstructionQuoted: "MULTIPLE DEFINITIONS (equally mandatory - a frequent real mistake): ... When your supplied source contains multiple independently meaningful defined terms, extract EVERY materially relevant definition supported by the supplied source - never select only the representative, salient, or apparently covenant-relevant ones and silently drop the rest. Emit one WireDefinition per distinct defined term you find, exactly as you would emit one WireRule per independently operative rule."

unitA2_deterministicCompletenessCheck.mechanism: Regex-based detection of the '"Term" means'/'"Term" shall mean' citation syntax in the supplied source text (the same operativeSourceText the model itself received - never a wider span). Compares detected term labels (normalized: trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, lowercased) against the compiled output's own termName labels. Fires ONLY when at least one detected term is absent from the compiled set; never fires merely because zero citations were detected (many valid sections - rules-only, single-definition - legitimately produce zero detections).
unitA2_deterministicCompletenessCheck.scopeDiscipline: Purely syntactic pattern matching - never interprets legal meaning, never infers what a missing definition says, never maintains a legal-term dictionary or enumerated covenant-concept list. Generalizes across covenant families and arbitrary/invented terminology by construction (verified in Unit A6's test using deliberately invented terms).
unitA2_deterministicCompletenessCheck.wiring: compile.ts calls checkDefinitionCompleteness(input.operativeSourceText, normalized.definitions) after normalization; a fired result pushes the new failureReason DEFINITION_COMPLETENESS_SUSPECT, which routes through the EXISTING determineStatus function exactly like every other failure reason (forces at least REVIEW_REQUIRED, never a new/different status kind, never manufactures IR content for the missing term).
unitA2_deterministicCompletenessCheck.resultField: SemanticCompilationResult.definitionCompletenessCheck (optional, mirrors the established inputHasUnresolvedOperativeEvidence convention for backward compatibility with pre-existing test fixtures/mocks) - null when the check found nothing, the full diagnostic object when it fired.

unitA3_truncationIntegrity.tracedRootCause: Five candidate mechanisms were checked per the mission's own taxonomy. SOURCE TRUNCATION: not evidenced either way (outside this investigation's scope - would require the raw source/candidate boundary). CONTEXT-WINDOW TRUNCATION: ruled out for the primary operativeSourceText (built via unbounded index.getNodeText and passed to the model with no truncation in caller.ts); PLAUSIBLE for follow-up tool-call results, which ARE capped at semantic/tools.ts's MAX_TEXT_RESULT_CHARS=4000. MODEL OUTPUT TRUNCATION: a real mechanism exists (stop_reason==='max_tokens' -> recoverPartialSubmission), but it behaves as a structured whole-item drop with an explicit marker, not a silent mid-clause ellipsis inside an otherwise-valid COMPLETE definition - an unlikely exact match. POST-PROCESSING TRUNCATION: ruled out (normalize.ts/wire-schema.ts never truncate/slice/cap any string). DISPLAY-ONLY TRUNCATION: no such layer exists in the backend files inspected.
unitA3_truncationIntegrity.mostPlausibleExplanation: The RGT-C-022 Riot ellipsis most likely originated as the model's OWN generated text (its own abbreviating excerpt, or a paraphrase of a getDefinition/getReferencedProvision tool result already truncated at the 4000-char ceiling) - not any of the four backend mechanisms. This is disclosed as inferred, not directly proven, since it would require the raw model transcript for that specific historical call, which this remediation does not have and does not attempt to re-derive (Riot GT/source/thresholds remain immutable per governing constraints).
unitA3_truncationIntegrity.fixImplemented: Rather than raising the 4000-char limit (explicitly forbidden by the mission - 'do NOT solve this merely by increasing one global token or character limit'), made truncation an explicit, STRUCTURED signal that participates in the safe-failure gate, independent of whether the model's own JSON reading of the `truncated: true` field influences its behavior. Added ToolExecutionOutcome.evidenceTruncated / ToolCallLogEntry.evidenceTruncated (mirroring the existing evidenceUnresolved pattern exactly), set at all 9 real truncate() call sites in tools.ts (getOperativeProvision x2, getDefinition, getParentClause, getSiblingClauses (any-sibling-truncated), getReferencedProvision x2, getPriorVersion, getSourceSpan). compile.ts now pushes a new failureReason TRUNCATED_EVIDENCE_USED whenever any tool call this attempt made returned truncated text, forcing at least REVIEW_REQUIRED via the same existing determineStatus machinery - so a definition/qualifier read off truncated evidence can never be silently treated as complete merely because it happened to validate against the IR schema.
unitA3_truncationIntegrity.continuationRetryDecision: No continuation/retry mechanism was added - the codebase's own prior explicit rejection of a 'full decomposition/continuation' architecture (caller.ts's header comment, from the original 8192-to-128000-token-ceiling fix) is directly on point and this remediation does not revisit that judgment. Truncated evidence is made explicit and safety-gated, not retried or expanded.

antiEnumerationCompliance: Both A1 (prompt instruction) and A2 (regex detector) are general mechanisms with no enumerated legal terms, section numbers, or package names anywhere - verified they would behave identically under arbitrary invented terminology (Unit A6 test) and generalize across multiple definitions in one section, embedded conditions, and sibling subclauses by construction (pattern matches citation SYNTAX, not term SEMANTICS).
